 The NWS Los Angeles-Oxnard office is estimating a 30% to 40% chance of thunderstorms with widespread minor flooding and debris flow concerns in Los Angeles and Ventura counties.
 The biggest risk of concern for flooding, according to a weather service spokesperson, is in the Santa Monica Mountains.
 That percentage drops to 15% to 25% in Orange, Riverside, San Bernardino and San Diego counties.
 p]:text-cms-story-body-color-text" data-subscriber-content> Rain is anticipated for Southern California on Wednesday into Thursday as the National Weather Service cautioned about potential beach hazards and thunderstorms from Oxnard to the Mexico border.
 The weather service’s Los Angeles-Oxnard office is estimating a 30% to 40% chance of thunderstorms, with widespread minor flooding and debris flow concerns in L.A. and Ventura counties.
 Most areas, however, will probably experience only minor impacts from this weather, the office said.
 Advertisement California 
 Cooler temperatures, possible rain headed for Southern California 
 Cooler temperatures and a chance of rain is on tap for Southern California, forecasters say.
 Oct. 19, 2026 The area at highest risk for flooding is the Santa Monica Mountains, according to a weather service spokesperson.
 “Some of the more vulnerable areas include first-year burn scars,” a spokesperson said.
 The Palisades and Altadena areas are among those recently scarred by wildfires.
 As for rain amounts, the weather service in L.A. is expecting 1.73 inches of rain in Thousand Oaks from Wednesday into Thursday, with Oxnard at 1.53 inches, Santa Clarita at 1.47 inches, LAX at 1.31 inches, Covina at 1.29 inches and Long Beach at just under an inch.
 (National Weather Service) Advertisement At beaches in the L.A. County and Oxnard region, surf of 3 to 6 feet is expected through Thursday night on south- and southwest-facing beaches.
 Tides are expected to range from 5.5 to 6.2 feet.
 The weather service’s San Diego office, which monitors Orange, San Bernardino, Riverside and San Diego counties, issued a beach hazard warning on Tuesday at 1:30 p.m.
 The notice, in effect until 11 p.m. , cautions about dangerous rip currents and breaking waves, with surf from 3 to 6 feet. The highest surf is expected on south- and southwest-facing beaches, according to NWS San Diego.
 Climate & Environment 
 Major loss of California beaches predicted in latest climate forecast 
 Southern California is on track to lose 30 to 70% of its beaches over the next several decades. Almost half of all beach cliffs are likely to retreat by 30 to 80 feet by 2100.
 Oct. 20, 2026 The agency is warning that rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea, while waves can wash people off beaches and rocks and capsize small boats near shore.
 The weather service is advising swimmers to “remain out of the water to avoid hazardous swimming conditions.”
 A map shows expected rain amounts in the San Diego County region. (National Weather Service) Advertisement The chance of rain on Wednesday morning and afternoon stands at about 53% in Irvine and Anaheim and 46% in San Clemente, while Ontario is at 44% and Riverside, 40%.
 The chance of precipitation picks up, however, Wednesday evening into Thursday morning, with Anaheim, Irvine and San Clemente at 95%, Ontario at 92%, Riverside and Lake Elsinore at 91% and San Bernardino at 88%.
 The National Weather Service in San Diego is warning of a potential 15% to 25% widespread chance, or moderate risk, of thunderstorms throughout all four counties.
